rapport_notes: Joanna is warm, conversational, uses customer's name, and maintains a calm helpful tone throughout; minor hesitations and slight audio clarity issues prevent a perfect score.
process_discipline_notes: No silence after 'does that make sense?' (rep continues immediately); no silence after 'does that feel fair?' (rep pivots to estimate without pause).

evidence_quotes.agenda: Joanna: 'But before we start I just wanna ask what would be your, like, major concerns about moving in general about this move that you also want us to discuss over the phone today?' Asked before logistics probing.
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: Zach raises downsizing concern ('most of the furniture...half the size of the house'). Joanna acknowledges and offers a video call but does not probe deeper into the downsizing concern itself—no 'tell me more' or 'what else.' Follow-up is shallow and pivots to solution (video call) rather than layering.
evidence_quotes.save_your_ass: Estimate is a window: 'So again it might still change depending on your final list.' Beats it pay less: 'If we go over we only charge in fifteen minute interval so we don't charge you for the full hour right away. So it's every fifteen minutes after the minimum.' Self-prep tip: NOT mentioned. Commit to rate: NOT mentioned. Does that feel fair + silence: NOT executed (rep says 'Alright' and moves to estimate without waiting).

top_strength: Joanna delivers a clear, comprehensive pricing explanation that covers damage coverage ($2,000), Meet Your Mover (crew names in advance), and On-Time Guarantee (discounts if late) all in one coherent block, giving the customer a complete value picture.
coaching_note: After asking open-ended questions ('does that make sense?' and 'does that feel fair?'), hold silence and let the customer respond—do not immediately re-pitch or explain; also, dig one layer deeper into Zach's downsizing concern instead of jumping to the video-call solution.
